Recommended direction · The Courier

A public purpose.
A little personality.

An attentive little bird, carrying the record into reach. An emblem for a product that makes local government easier to follow—and easier to act on.

The public-record courier
Politic Public · Proposed signature
politicpublic

Come prepared.

Ink color

The established wordmark keeps its clarity. The new symbol gives the identity something you can remember and describe.

Information, in public hands.

The document makes the bird’s purpose specific. It carries useful information from a public meeting into someone’s working day. That connects the professional product to the wider public mission.

Attentive. Capable. Approachable.

The upright tail and forward stance give it alertness. Its small, local character adds warmth to the calm authority of the type. It belongs comfortably beside a serious legislative brief.

Drawn with intention.

Unequal tail shapes, a scooped wing, and slightly awkward feet make the silhouette feel authored. The personality comes from the contour; it does not depend on distressed texture or extra decoration.

In context

A signature with a job.

Use it as a quiet sign of authorship on the landing page, meeting briefs, and correspondence.

Small-size study. At favicon scale, the eye, paper fold, and feet need a simpler optical version. These PNGs are concept artwork, ahead of the final vector drawing.

Alternative · The Open Record

A more abstract civic mark.

Two uneven pages open around a central passage. The intention is access: a public record that can be entered, understood, and used.

This is compact and composed, but the meaning needs more explanation. The Courier has the more distinctive character and the stronger connection to delivering useful information.
